passages.text: If the provider status lookup is unavailable, the payment stays in reconciliation. An unavailable lookup is not proof that a transfer failed. The worker continues checking with capped backoff; ask operations to investigate a prolonged incident.

A reconciling payment has an uncertain provider outcome, often because a response was lost after acceptance. The worker checks the provider using the original idempotency key. Do not create a replacement payment while the outcome is unknown.

Manual retry is unavailable for reconciling payments. Retry is allowed only after three explicit failures before provider acceptance. An unknown outcome must be resolved through authoritative provider lookup or a verified callback.

evidence.title: What this demo can and cannot do
evidence.heading: Support assistant scope
evidence.text: SourceDesk explains the published synthetic support guides. It cannot inspect your bank, retrieve live balances, approve a payment, or change credentials. Account-specific payment status, disputes, missing funds, and undocumented policies require human review.

evidence.title: Diagnosing service health
evidence.heading: Liveness and readiness
evidence.text: The health endpoint reports that the API process is alive. The readiness endpoint also checks PostgreSQL, the provider, and a recent worker heartbeat when jobs exist. A 503 readiness response indicates a degraded dependency or stale worker.

evidence.title: What this demo can and cannot do
evidence.heading: Synthetic payments only
evidence.text: LedgerDesk uses fictional companies, recipients, and transfers. No real money moves. It does not connect to a bank, issue refunds, calculate fees or tax, or promise real-world settlement times.
